record_identity.title: Deepfake of Western Australia Premier Roger Cook used in investment scam

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Deepfake of Western Australia Premier Roger Cook used in investment scam
incident_identity.date_basis: ABC News reported the Western Australian government warning on 8 November 2025.

summary: A fraudulent YouTube advertisement used an AI-generated likeness and voice of Western Australian Premier Roger Cook to promote an investment scheme as government-backed. Cook and the Western Australian Consumer Protection Commissioner rejected the endorsement and warned that the advertisement was fraudulent; the reporting reviewed for this record did not identify any realised victim loss.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: ABC News preserved the government's warning and described a YouTube pop-up advertisement that imitated Roger Cook's appearance and voice. The Premier and Consumer Protection Commissioner rejected the endorsement and warned that the material was fraudulent. The reviewed evidence does not establish a realised victim loss.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The advertisement treated a synthetic representation of a public official as carrying the official's actual endorsement authority. The incident materialised impersonation and correction burden, while financial harm remains attempted rather than established.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The case illustrates how synthetic public-office identity can be used to manufacture institutional credibility for fraud even where downstream monetary loss is not yet evidenced.
assessment_boundaries: No reviewed source establishes that a viewer transferred money or sustained financial loss.
The record does not infer how the advertisement was generated beyond the reported synthetic voice and likeness.
